markup.title: Write an HTTP Request
code_lines: # Write the HTTP method to request a homepage
mission_steps: Write a GET request for the /home/ path
Why: HTTP GET is the fundamental method that all browsers use to retrieve web pages from servers.
markup.error_output: 400 Bad Request — Check your HTTP method and path format!
progressive_hints: The format is 'METHOD PATH PROTOCOL'.
Use 'GET' for the METHOD, and '/home/' for the PATH.
Use 'HTTP/1.1' as the PROTOCOL.

mission_steps:

, and

tags
Why: HTML provides the core structure of the web. Headings and paragraphs define the semantic meaning of the text.
markup.error_output: SyntaxError: Missing or mismatched tags — check your angle brackets!

Use '

' for 'Hello' and '

markup.title: Style a Box
code_lines: /* Style the div to have proper spacing */
mission_steps: Add margin: 20px; and padding: 10px; to the box
Why: CSS controls visual layout. The Box Model (margins and padding) determines how elements are spaced.
markup.error_output: Error: Invalid CSS property — check your syntax (property: value;)
progressive_hints: The format is 'property: value;'.
Set 'margin: 20px;' and 'padding: 10px;'.
Don't forget the semicolons at the end of each rule.

markup.title: Center with Flexbox
code_lines: /* Center the items in this container */
/* Make this a flex container and center items */
mission_steps: Add display: flex; and justify-content: center;
Why: Flexbox is a modern CSS layout module that allows you to easily align and distribute elements dynamically.
markup.correct_output: ✅ Items are now centered using Flexbox!
markup.error_output: Error: Invalid layout — make sure you use display: flex first!
progressive_hints: The format is 'display: type;' and 'justify-content: alignment;'.
Set display to 'flex'.
Set justify-content to 'center'.

markup.title: Write a Media Query
code_lines: /* Make the layout responsive for small screens */
/* Write a media query for screens 600px or smaller */
mission_steps: Write a media query for max-width: 600px
Why: Media queries allow your website to adapt its CSS responsively so it looks good on both phones and desktops.
markup.correct_output: ✅ Media query active — layout adapts for small screens!
markup.error_output: Error: Invalid media query syntax — check your @media rule!
progressive_hints: The format is '@media (condition) {}'.
Use 'max-width: 600px' as the condition inside the parentheses.
Ensure the curly braces are placed correctly.

syntax.title: Write a For Loop
code_lines: # Write a for loop that prints 0 to 4
# Use range() to generate the numbers
mission_steps: Write a for loop using range(5) that prints each number
Why: Loops automate repetitive tasks, allowing you to process lists or run code multiple times instantly.
syntax.error_output: SyntaxError: invalid syntax — check your for loop structure!
progressive_hints: The format is 'for variable in range(n):'.
Use 'i' as your variable, and 'range(5)' for the numbers.
Indent the next line and use the print function.

syntax.title: Create a Class
code_lines: # Create a Student class with a constructor
# The constructor should accept 'name' as a parameter
mission_steps: Define class Student with __init__(self, name) that stores self.name
Why: Classes act as blueprints. They let you create objects that bundle data and behavior, which is how Django builds its structures.
syntax.error_output: SyntaxError: invalid class definition — check your indentation and colons!
progressive_hints: The format is 'class ClassName:'.
The constructor format is 'def __init__(self, param):'.
Inside the constructor, assign the parameter using 'self.param = param'.

syntax.title: Make an HTTP Request
code_lines: # Make a GET request to the URL below
mission_steps: Write a GET request using requests.get() with the given URL
Why: Making HTTP requests allows your code to talk to APIs and other servers to retrieve live data over the web.
syntax.error_output: ConnectionError: Could not reach the server — check your URL and method!
progressive_hints: The format is 'response = requests.get(url)'.
Pass the URL string as the argument inside the parentheses.
Assign the result of the function call to a variable named 'response'.

view.title: Create a Virtual Environment
code_lines: # Create a new virtual environment called 'venv'
mission_steps: Type the command to create a venv named 'venv'
Why: Virtual environments isolate your project's packages so they don't conflict with other Python projects on your computer.
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid command — use python -m venv <name>
progressive_hints: Run the python module associated with virtual environments.
Specify the standard library module with the '-m' flag: '-m venv'.
Provide the same name for the directory to hold the environment: 'venv'.

view.title: Activate the Virtual Environment
code_lines: # Your virtual environment 'venv' has been created
mission_steps: Type the command to activate the venv
Why: Activating the environment ensures that any packages you install or run are contained within this specific sandbox.
view.correct_output:
✅ Virtual environment activated!
  (venv) C:\Users\hansu\Documents\Capstone\DjangoQuest-Backend> _
  All pip installs will now go into venv/
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid activation command — use venv\Scripts\activate
progressive_hints: Run the activate script located within the environment folder.
It sits inside 'venv', then inside the 'Scripts' directory.
Check your backslashes for the Windows path.

view.title: Install Django
code_lines: # Install the Django framework using pip
# Make sure your venv is activated first!
mission_steps: Type the pip command to install Django
Why: pip is Python's package manager. Installing Django gives you the framework needed to build powerful web applications.
view.correct_output:
✅ Collecting django
  Downloading Django-5.0-py3-none-any.whl (8.1 MB)
Successfully installed Django-5.0 asgiref-3.7.2 sqlparse-0.4.4
view.error_output: ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement. Check your command.
progressive_hints: Your package manager is called 'pip'.
Combine the 'install' command with the name of the framework.
Ensure you spell 'django' correctly.

view.title: Create a Django Project
code_lines: # Create a new Django project called 'mysite'
mission_steps: Type the command to create a Django project named 'mysite'
Why: django-admin creates the foundational folder structure and settings files required for every Django app.
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid command — use django-admin startproject <name>
progressive_hints: Use the django-admin tool.
Combine it with the startproject action.
Provide 'mysite' as the name parameter.

view.title: Navigate to Project Folder
code_lines: # Navigate into your newly created project directory!
mission_steps: Type the command to change directories into 'mysite'
Why: manage.py exists only inside the 'mysite' folder. You can't use it if you are not inside the correct folder.
progressive_hints: The command to change directory contains two letters.
Pass the name of the project folder to it.

view.title: Migrate Database
mission_steps: Type the manage.py command to migrate the database
Why: 'migrate' prepares the default database tables needed by Django for things like users and sessions.
view.correct_output:
✅ Operations to perform:
  Apply all migrations: admin, auth, contenttypes, sessions
Running migrations:
  Applying contenttypes.0001_initial... OK
  Applying auth.0001_initial... OK
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid command — use python manage.py migrate
progressive_hints: Your project's command center is manage.py.
Execute manage.py with python and append 'migrate'.

view.title: Start the Server
mission_steps: Type the command to start the server
Why: The dev server runs your code locally on port 8000 so you can test your app in the browser.
view.correct_output:
✅ Django version 5.0, using settings 'mysite.settings'
Starting development server at http://127.0.0.1:8000/
Quit the server with CONTROL-C.
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid command — use python manage.py runserver
progressive_hints: Run the manage.py script using Python.
Pass 'runserver' as the argument.

view.title: Create a Django App
code_lines: # Create a new app called 'blog' inside your project
mission_steps: Type the command to create a Django app named 'blog'
Why: Projects are built out of smaller apps (like 'store' or 'blog') to keep code organized and modular.
view.error_output: CommandError: invalid command — use python manage.py startapp <name>
progressive_hints: Run manage.py using Python.
Use the action 'startapp' with the argument 'blog'.

view.title: Register Your App
code_lines: # Add your app name below as a string:
mission_steps: Add 'blog' to the INSTALLED_APPS list
Why: Django won't recognize your new app until it is explicitly registered in the project's central settings file.
view.placeholder: Type the app name as a string...
view.correct_output:
✅ App 'blog' registered!
  Django now recognizes your app.
  Models, views, and templates will be loaded.
view.error_output: Error: App not found. Did you add it as a string?
progressive_hints: Add the app name as a Python string
Type: 'blog'

view.title: Load Static Files
mission_steps: Inspect `settings.py` for STATIC_URL
Open `templates/base.html`
Add `{% load static %}` at the very top
Why: Static files like CSS and images are never served automatically. They must be explicitly loaded in templates.
view.correct_output:
✅ Static files loaded!
  CSS and JS are now available in your template.
view.error_output: TemplateSyntaxError: 'static' is not a registered tag — did you forget {% load static %}?
progressive_hints: Django requires you to explicitly bring in the static file system.
Use the Django template tag syntax '{% %}' to load the 'static' library.
This tag must be placed at the very top of the HTML file.

view.title: Generic ListView (Read All)
mission_steps: Use ListView to display all Books, route it with as_view(), and render object_list.
Why: Because Django's ORM and Views are heavily abstracted for speed of development.
view.correct_output: ✅ Success! ListView successfully routed and rendered.
view.error_output: Error: Ensure you hit all 3 files. Use BookListView in urls, and object_list in the template.
progressive_hints: In views.py, specify the 'model' attribute to link the view to the Book class.
In urls.py, call the as_view() method on your generic view class to use it as a route handler.
In book_list.html, iterate through 'object_list' using a Django template loop.

view.title: Generic DetailView (Read Single)
mission_steps: Use an integer parameter in the URL route to pass the Primary Key to the DetailView.
Why: DetailView inherently relies on URL parameters to safely query the exact database record requested.
view.correct_output: ✅ Success! DetailView successfully routed via Primary Key.
view.error_output: Error: Use <int:pk> in the URL path, and BookDetailView.as_view().
progressive_hints: Construct a path starting with 'book/', followed by the primary key integer parameter '<int:pk>/'.
Route it to the BookDetailView using the as_view() method.
Optionally provide a name for the route, such as 'book-detail'.

view.title: Generic CreateView (Create Data)
mission_steps: Use CreateView to orchestrate form creation and redirection.
Why: Without specifying fields and success_url, CreateView does not know what data to permit or where to send the user after saving.
view.error_output: Error: Specify 'fields' as a list containing 'name', and reverse_lazy for the success_url.
progressive_hints: Initialize the 'fields' list containing just the 'name' string.
Set 'success_url' to the result of 'reverse_lazy' pointing to the 'books' route.

query.title: Define a Model Field
code_lines: # Define a name field using a CharField with max_length=100
mission_steps: Define the 'name' field using models.CharField(max_length=100)
Why: Models define your database schema in Python code. Django automatically translates this class into full SQL database tables.
query.correct_output:
✅ Success! Table column 'name' defined.
  Column type: VARCHAR(100)
  Nullable: False
query.error_output: Error: Invalid Field Definition. Did you use models.CharField?
progressive_hints: The format is 'field_name = models.FieldType(parameter=value)'.
Use 'name' as the field name, and 'models.CharField' as the type.
Set 'max_length=100' inside the CharField parentheses.

query.title: Guess The Field Mapping
code_lines: # 1. Stores a short Title string (max length 200)
# 2. Stores a gigantic text block (unlimited length)
mission_steps: Fill in the missing field types (models.CharField, models.TextField, models.BooleanField)
Why: Matching the right type to the data requirement ensures efficient, uncorrupted SQL mapping.
query.correct_output: ✅ Success! Fields mapped properly to VARCHAR, TEXT, and BOOLEAN.
query.error_output: Error: Invalid Field Definition. Check spelling and capitalization.
progressive_hints: The format for fields is 'models.FieldType(options)'.
Title is 'models.CharField(max_length=200)', Synopsis is 'models.TextField()'.
is_published should be 'models.BooleanField()'.

query.title: Extract Specific Data
code_lines: # Use ORM to get all students whose grade is 'A'
mission_steps: Write: Student.objects.filter(grade='A')
Why: Filtering allows you to efficiently retrieve only the specific records you need, rather than loading the entire database into memory.
query.correct_output:
✅ QuerySet generated successfully!
  <QuerySet [<Student: Alice>, <Student: Bob>]>
  2 records matched.
query.error_output: Error: QuerySet invalid. Use the model's objects manager.
progressive_hints: The format is 'Model.objects.filter(field=value)'.
Use 'Student' as the model and 'grade' as the field.
Set the grade equal to the string 'A'.

query.title: Register to Admin
mission_steps: Type admin.site.register(Student)
Why: Registering your model tells Django to automatically generate a graphical CRUD interface for it in the /admin/ panel.
query.correct_output:
✅ Success! Student Model registered.
  Admin panel: /admin/blog/student/
  Actions: Add, Change, Delete, View
query.error_output: Error: Not registered correctly. Did you use admin.site.register?
progressive_hints: The format is 'admin.site.register(ModelClass)'.
Pass 'Student' into the parentheses to register it.

query.title: Complete the View
code_lines: # Retrieve ALL student records to pass to the template
mission_steps: Use ORM to extract all records using objects.all()
Why: The ORM lets you retrieve data from the database using Python objects instead of writing raw SQL queries.
query.error_output: Error: Could not retrieve records. Use objects.all()
progressive_hints: The format is 'Model.objects.all()'.
Use the 'Student' model to retrieve all records.

token.title: Define a ModelForm
code_lines: # Define the Meta class linking to the Student model
mission_steps: Define class Meta with model = Student and fields = ['name', 'grade']
Why: ModelForms automatically generate HTML forms based on your database models, saving you from writing repetitive validation logic.
token.correct_output:
✅ ModelForm created successfully!
  Linked to: Student
  Fields: name, grade
  Validation: Active
token.error_output: Error: Invalid ModelForm — check your Meta class definition!
progressive_hints: Start with: class Meta:
Inside Meta, set: model = Student
Then set: fields = ['name', 'grade']

token.title: Add CSRF Protection
mission_steps: Add the {% csrf_token %} template tag
Why: The CSRF token protects your forms from Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks, ensuring submissions actually come from your own site.
token.correct_output:
✅ CSRF token added!
  Form is now protected against Cross-Site Request Forgery.
  Token: Unique per session, verified on submit.
token.error_output: SecurityError: CSRF token missing — your form is vulnerable!
progressive_hints: Use a Django template tag: {% ... %}
The tag name is: csrf_token
Type: {% csrf_token %}

token.title: Send a Success Message
code_lines: # Send a success message to the user
mission_steps: Write: messages.success(request, 'Saved!')
Why: The messages framework lets you queue one-time notifications that automatically display to users on the next page load.
token.correct_output:
✅ Message queued!
  Type: SUCCESS
  Text: "Saved!"
  Will display on next page render.
token.error_output: Error: Invalid message call — use messages.success(request, 'text')
progressive_hints: Import is already done. Use: messages.success()
Pass two arguments: request and the message string
Type: messages.success(request, 'Saved!')

auth.title: Authenticate a User
code_lines: # Authenticate the user with the provided credentials
mission_steps: Write: authenticate(request, username=username, password=password)
Why: The authenticate function is Django's secure way to verify that a username and password match a valid user in the database.
auth.correct_output:
✅ Authentication successful!
  User: alice
  Session: Started
  Status: Logged in
auth.error_output: AuthenticationError: Invalid credentials — check your authenticate() call!
progressive_hints: The format is 'user = authenticate(request, username=variable, password=variable)'.
Fill in the two variable arguments with the data from the request.

auth.title: Check Ownership
code_lines: # Check if the current user owns this post
mission_steps: Write: if request.user == post.owner:
Why: Checking ownership ensures that logged-in users can only modify their own data, preventing unauthorized edits.
auth.correct_output:
✅ Permission check passed!
  User: alice
  Post Owner: alice
  Action: Allowed
auth.error_output: PermissionError: Ownership check failed — use request.user == object.owner
progressive_hints: The format is 'if condition:'.
The condition should be 'request.user == object.owner'.
Substitute 'post.owner' for the object's owner.

auth.title: Create a Custom User Model
mission_steps: Extend AbstractUser and add a 'phone' field, then register it in settings.py.
Why: The default User model cannot be modified after the first migration. AbstractUser lets you define custom fields from the start.
auth.correct_output:
✅ CustomUser model created with phone field!
  AUTH_USER_MODEL set correctly.
auth.error_output: Error: Ensure you inherit from AbstractUser and set AUTH_USER_MODEL.
progressive_hints: In models.py format: 'class CustomUser(AbstractUser): phone = models.CharField(...)'.
In settings.py format: 'AUTH_USER_MODEL = "app.Model"'.

auth.title: Hash a Password
code_lines: # Use the method that automatically hashes it
mission_steps: Use set_password() to securely change a user's password.
Why: set_password() runs the raw string through Django's hashing algorithm (PBKDF2 + SHA256) before storing it, ensuring no plaintext password ever touches the database.
auth.correct_output:
✅ Password updated!
  Hash: pbkdf2_sha256$260000$...
  Raw password is NEVER stored.
auth.error_output: Error: Don't assign password directly. Use set_password().
progressive_hints: The format is 'user.set_password("password")'.
Pass the new password 'new_secure_pass' as the string argument.

rest.title: Create a ModelSerializer
mission_steps: Write: fields = ['id', 'title', 'content']
Why: Serializers translate complex database models into simple formats like JSON, making the data ready to be transmitted over an API.
rest.correct_output:
✅ Serializer created successfully!
  PostSerializer → Post model
  Fields: id, title, content
  Output: {"id": 1, "title": "Hello", "content": "World"}
rest.error_output: SerializerError: Invalid field definition — check your fields list!
progressive_hints: The format is 'fields = ["field1", "field2", "field3"]'.
Define the fields variable as a list of strings.
The list should contain 'id', 'title', and 'content'.

rest.title: Configure Token Authentication
mission_steps: Write: 'rest_framework.authentication.TokenAuthentication',
Why: Adding this to DRF settings tells the API to expect and validate token-based authentication headers from clients.
rest.correct_output:
✅ Token Authentication configured!
  DRF Settings Updated
  Auth Class: TokenAuthentication
  All API endpoints now require a valid token.
rest.error_output: ConfigurationError: Invalid auth class — check the path to TokenAuthentication!
progressive_hints: The format is '"module.path.ClassName",'.
Add the string 'rest_framework.authentication.TokenAuthentication' to the list.
Don't forget the quotes and comma.

rest.title: Build a ViewSet & Router
mission_steps: Create a ModelViewSet with queryset and serializer_class, then register it with a Router.
Why: ViewSets eliminate the need to write individual API views for each CRUD operation. One class handles list, create, retrieve, update, and delete.
rest.correct_output:
✅ Full REST API generated!
  GET    /api/posts/      → List
  POST   /api/posts/      → Create
  GET    /api/posts/{id}/  → Retrieve
  PUT    /api/posts/{id}/  → Update
  DELETE /api/posts/{id}/  → Delete
rest.error_output: Error: Ensure queryset and serializer_class are set, and the router registers the viewset.
progressive_hints: In views.py format: 'queryset = Model.objects.all()' and 'serializer_class = ModelSerializer'.
In urls.py format: 'router.register("prefix", ViewSet)'.
Register 'posts' to PostViewSet.
